*This WAF to replace WAF # XBTX88-492526 (job # 009T78971) with updated job number (012T91171 ).    ____________________________________________  Circuit A flat   6/22-Called out for warranty flat circuit. Picked up material to leak test. Put trace gas in system and pumped up with nitrogen found leak on condenser coil. There is no sign of physical damage or user misuse. Coil needs to be replaced. Leak checked the other components in machine found none. Put unit back in service running only B circuit.  8/23-Picked up reclaim cylinder and checked in with customer. Spoke about the progression of the job and performed a walk through. Spoke about the crane lift and where it will set up as well as how long system is expected to be down. Removed refrigerant from system. Left system powered so that customer can have fan circulation. Returned reclaim cylinder and picked up various materials from different locations for repair of leaking circuit. Will return tomorrow to continue job.  8/24-Arrived at job site and checked in with customer. Roped off area for the crane to setup and began disassembly of unit. Removed the panels necessary to cut pipes back and to slide the coil out of unit. When crane arrived spoke about the pick with operator and began removing the crating to verify coil. Found no major damage to new coil. Rigged up new coil and placed on roof and also sent old coil down for transport back to the shop. Crated old coil up and crane company delivered it back to the shop for warranty. Moved new coil into place and brazed each line. Reinstalled all brackets and panels and placed system on a vacuum pump. Pump will run all night to pulled system down and we will check microns in the morning. Checked out with the customer.  8/24- (2nd Tech): Checked in with customer. Brought tools up to roof. Disconnected unit structure and shored up with wood. Unbrazed coil. Took out coil. Waited for new coil and crane to arrive. Craned up new coil. Uncrated coil. Put old coil in crate. Craned down old coil. Installed new coil. Braze

RTU#3 has alarm for T111 Circuit B loss of charge. Needed to perform leak check on Circuit B.  Performed leak search on Circuit B and located leak with electronic leak detector and confirmed with soap bubbles on condenser coil.  Replaced leaking coil with new coil.

I found the compressor skid not screw to the rooftop unit. The large u-channel base with all 4 compressors on it was not screw to anything, not one screw! It had slid around a little in transit. I re-positioned and screwed down. Then with the gas heat there was a limit switch in the blower section that had one of the two wires hanging loose and the other retaining screw was about to come off. I reconnected and tightened.

Meet with technician from Peterson mechanical. Power is out at building and surrounding area. Unable to access equipment. Need to reschedule warranty service call. Informed office of situation.    Meet at site with Peterson mechanical, installing contractor. Found 3rd floor unit #3 with grounded A-1 digital scroll compressor. Acid test done and is bad burn . Talked with factory, Alan Henderson on proper system clean up needed, will need dip tube tool from RC to get contaminated oil from tandem compressor. Order all components needed for repairs. Defective crankcase heater , compressor contactor.    Picked up two new compressors and all parts needed for replacement.    Picked up tri pod and rigging from shop. Drive to sure and hauled compressors onto roof and dropped the old ones. Cleaned site.    Warranty. Remove and replace two compressors. Digital scroll grounded. Replace filter drier. Nitrogen charge overnight.     Return to site, system pressures held overnight. Installed vacuum pump and triple evacuate. Microns at 1250 and decided to keep pump on overnight. Purged again with nitrogen. Installed new compressor contactor, crankcase heater and reinstalled digital scroll solenoid coil.  Will return tomorrow.    System at 430 microns. Add factory charge of 43# of 410a . Raining again.  Start up and test operation of all components. Check oil levels, recommend follow up to test oil and refrigerant status .
